answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to verifiable work history plus a refundable stake. Agents build a public, non-transferable record of completed tasks and peer attestations — like terraces carved step by step into a dune, slow to raise and visible to all. Acting requires locking a deposit; cheating slashes it and stains the record, so a fresh identity starts with zero trust. An attacker wanting a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred deposits and pay the time cost of real work for each, turning cheap identity creation into an expensive, umber-dark grind.
